title: Finite type for a coordinatewise surjective product pullback
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I$ be a finite set, and let $Q$, $C_i$, and $D_i$ for $i\in I$ be commutative finite type $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Suppose $\varphi_i:C_i\to D_i$ and $\psi_i:Q\to D_i$ are surjective $R$-algebra homomorphisms for every $i$. Give the subset $T=\{(q,(c_i))\in Q\times\prod_{i\in I}C_i\mid\psi_i(q)=\varphi_i(c_i)\text{ for every }i\}$ its componentwise $R$-algebra operations. Then $T$ is of finite type over $R$. For $I=\varnothing$ the product is the one-element ring and $T\cong Q$.

source.place: Tag 08NI (lemma-formal-consequence), cartesian square with both coordinate maps surjective; proof uses lemma-fibre-product-finite-type and induction on the finite index set.

proof.text: Induct on $|I|$, for all data in the statement. For $I=\varnothing$, the map $q\mapsto(q,())$ identifies $Q$ with $T$ as an $R$-algebra, with inverse the first projection. Polynomial expressions for generators of $Q$ therefore give generators of $T$. More generally, for every $J\subseteq I$, write $T_J$ for the same subset using only $j\in J$. Its projection $p_J:T_J\to Q$ is surjective: given $q$, choose $c_j$ with $\varphi_j(c_j)=\psi_j(q)$ for each of the finitely many $j$.

source.place: Tag 08NI, lemma-formal-consequence, induction on the size of I; Tag 00IT, lemma-fibre-product-finite-type, Artin–Tate argument in the case of two surjections.

proof.text: For the induction step write $I=J\amalg\{i\}$. The induction hypothesis makes $A=T_J$ finite type over $R$. Set $C=C_i$, $D=D_i$ and $\alpha=\psi_i\circ p_J:A\to D$. Step 1 and surjectivity of $\psi_i$ make $\alpha$ surjective. The subalgebra $P=\{(a,c)\in A\times C\mid\alpha(a)=\varphi_i(c)\}$ is identified with $T$ by $((q,(c_j)_{j\in J}),c)\mapsto(q,(c_j)_{j\in J},c_i=c)$. Deleting the $i$th coordinate is its inverse; these maps preserve each componentwise operation and the scalar maps.

source.place: Tag 08NI, lemma-formal-consequence, induction on the size of I; Tag 00IT, lemma-fibre-product-finite-type, Artin–Tate argument in the case of two surjections.

proof.text: Put $B=A\times C$. Choose finite $R$-algebra generators $a_u$ for $A$ and $c_v$ for $C$. Then $(1,0),(0,1),(a_u,0),(0,c_v)$ generate $B$ as an $R$-algebra: if $a=f(a_u)$ and $c=g(c_v)$, then $(a,c)=(1,0)f((a_u,0))+(0,1)g((0,c_v))$, evaluating the polynomials using the diagonal scalar map $R\to B$. Thus $B$ is finite type over $R$.

source.place: Tag 08NI, lemma-formal-consequence, induction on the size of I; Tag 00IT, lemma-fibre-product-finite-type, Artin–Tate argument in the case of two surjections.

proof.text: Both projections $P\to A$ and $P\to C$ are surjective: lift $\alpha(a)$ along $\varphi_i$ for the first, and lift $\varphi_i(c)$ along $\alpha$ for the second. For $(a,c)\in B$ choose $(a,c^\prime),(a^\prime,c)\in P$. With the componentwise $P$-action, $(a,c)=(a,c^\prime)\cdot(1,0)+(a^\prime,c)\cdot(0,1)$. Hence $B$ is generated by $(1,0),(0,1)$ as a $P$-module, in the sense of [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Tag 08NI, lemma-formal-consequence, induction on the size of I; Tag 00IT, lemma-fibre-product-finite-type, Artin–Tate argument in the case of two surjections.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-artin-tate-subalgebra-finite-type] to the original Noetherian base $R$, the finite type algebra $B$ of Step 3, and its $R$-subalgebra $P$. Step 4 gives the required finite generation of $B$ as a $P$-module, so $P$ is finite type over $R$. The inverse maps of Step 2 send polynomial expressions in any finite generating set of $P$ to such expressions in $T$, proving the induction step and the assertion for every finite $I$.
